draft.title: Research and development
card: Research and development (R&D) is work that creates new products, or new and better ways to make things. It can raise productivity, which is the output produced from a given amount of resources.
Firms often spend less on R&D than is best for society. The results can spread to other firms, so the firm that pays for the research does not get all of the benefit.

The government can fund R&D through grants, such as money for university and CSIRO research. It can also use tax breaks, such as the R&D tax incentive, which lowers the tax a firm pays on eligible research spending.
These budget measures are supply-side policies. Over time, new methods and products can raise the economy's productive capacity and lower costs, though the gains can take years to appear.
draft.remember: R&D support lowers the cost of research for firms, so more new methods appear and productivity can rise over time.

a.q: Why might the government give tax breaks for R&D spending?
opts: Firms may invest too little, as others share the benefits
Firms always invest too much in research and need limits
Research raises demand immediately, so output rises at once
Tax breaks stop new firms copying products from other firms
a.why: The benefits of research can spread to other firms, so a firm may spend less than is best for society. A tax break lowers the firm's cost of research and encourages more of it. It does not lift output at once, because the gains take time.
a.clue: Think about who gets the benefit of a firm's research.

b.q: The government increases grants to university labs in Melbourne that develop new farming methods. Which result best shows a supply-side effect?
opts: Farms produce more per worker after adopting the methods
Farm workers spend more of their income on local goods
The grants cut the government's budget deficit that year
Farm prices rise because spending in the economy has risen
b.why: A supply-side effect is a rise in productivity and capacity, and more output per worker shows this. Higher spending by workers is a demand-side effect, which is the tempting wrong option. The grants are also spending, so they would not cut the deficit.
b.clue: Which result is about producing more from the same resources?

a.best: Firms may invest too little, as others share the benefits

b.best: Farms produce more per worker after adopting the methods
